skill.name: prove-it-ran
skill.description: Verify that tests, builds and checks actually ran and exercised the changed code, before claiming a task is done. Use before reporting completion, or when asked to prove tests ran or verify a fix.
skill.summary: Verify completion claims with fresh test output, regression checks, exit codes, and explicit reporting of unverified work.
skill.author: agentkitco

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks format an inline Markdown example, echo $?, which reads the previous command status. This is routine verification, not Ruby execution or command injection.
The Markdown example suggests temporarily stashing only the source fix, testing, and restoring it. This scoped regression workflow provides no evidence of malicious execution.
Backticks delimit skip markers and a fixed ripgrep search for disabled tests. The command inspects local test text without executing matched content.
Lines 29 through 35 contain a fenced Markdown table with illustrative verification results. The backticks are code fences, not executable shell substitutions.
Line 25 requests a table and honest disclosure of checks not run. It contains no system inspection command or reconnaissance instruction.
Line 39 requires command output as evidence or an admission that verification was not performed. This reporting rule does not request system reconnaissance.

content.user_title: Verify Tests Ran Before Reporting Completion
content.value_statement: Passing claims can hide skipped tests, stale results, or checks that never exercised a change. This skill guides fresh verification and evidence-based completion reports.
actual_capabilities: Guides fresh test runs and captures output for each completion claim.
Checks test counts, exit codes, test discovery, and changed test names.
Guides before-and-after regression testing by temporarily removing and restoring a source fix.
Checks output and source markers for skipped or focused tests.
Requests project-defined lint, type checks, and build verification.
Organizes claims, commands, evidence, and verification status in a report table.
limitations: Provides instructions, not a bundled test runner or automated verification service.
Requires access to project tools, dependencies, and an execution environment.
Before-and-after testing requires reversible source edits and may not be practical for every change.
Cannot verify checks requiring unavailable credentials, devices, or production access.

use_cases.title: Verify a bug fix
use_cases.description: Confirm the regression test fails without the fix and passes after restoration before closing a development task.

use_cases.title: Review completion evidence
use_cases.description: Check test discovery, skip markers, exit codes, and unverified claims before accepting a change.

use_cases.title: Prepare a release verification report
use_cases.description: Collect fresh test, lint, type check, and build evidence, with explicit notes for checks that cannot run.

prompt_templates.title: Verify one test run
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify that the relevant tests actually ran for my latest change. Report the command, test count, exit code, and anything unverified.

prompt_templates.title: Check discovery and skips
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the relevant tests and confirm changed tests appear in the output. Check discovery settings, skipped tests, and focused test markers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: investigate a suspicious passing result.

prompt_templates.title: Prove regression coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify this fix with a failing-before, passing-after test. Preserve unrelated edits, restore the fix, and report any verification limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: demonstrate that a regression test catches the bug.

prompt_templates.title: Audit all completion claims
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit every completion claim for this change. Run project-defined tests, lint, type checks, and builds; report exact commands, evidence, failures, and unverified items.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a complete handoff report.

output_examples.input: Verify whether my bug fix is covered by the regression test.
output: Illustrative result: the targeted test ran and failed with the source fix temporarily removed.
After restoring the fix, the same test passed with exit code zero.
The wider suite was not run, so overall suite status remains unverified.

output_examples.input: The test command exited successfully. Can I report that the tests passed?
output: Illustrative result: the runner reported zero tests, despite a successful exit code.
Test verification is incomplete because no test executed.
Check the working directory, runner configuration, and test filename pattern before rerunning.

output_examples.input: Summarize release verification when device checks are unavailable.
output: Illustrative result: the local suite ran 212 tests with no failures and exit code zero.
The build completed with exit code zero.
Not verified: device checks require unavailable hardware. Run the device checks on the target hardware before release.

best_practices: Rerun relevant checks after the latest edit and record exact commands with their output.
Preserve unrelated edits before temporarily removing a fix, and confirm restoration afterward.
Report failures and unavailable checks explicitly, with practical follow-up verification steps.
anti_patterns: Treating zero discovered tests or skipped tests as a successful test run.
Reusing stale output after changing files.
Editing tests, snapshots, or thresholds only to obtain a passing result.

faq.question: Does this skill include a test runner?
faq.answer: No. It guides the agent through verification using the commands and tools already available in your project.

faq.question: Is exit code zero enough to prove tests passed?
faq.answer: No. Confirm a nonzero test count, correct test discovery, and execution of the relevant tests.

faq.question: How does it check that a test covers a fix?
faq.answer: It asks for a failing run without the fix and a passing run after restoration, when that procedure is practical.

faq.question: What happens when a check cannot run?
faq.answer: The report marks it as not verified and explains how the user can check it.

faq.question: Can earlier test output support the final report?
faq.answer: Not after additional edits. The procedure requires fresh output for the current changes.

faq.question: How are unrelated failures reported?
faq.answer: Failures are reported in full. They are labeled pre-existing only after confirmation on a clean checkout.
